question: What claim is at stake in holding that poison does not enter the body even if one has been bitten by great serpents?
premises: A bite by great serpents is posited.
Poison is the usual agent in such a bite.
It is claimed that poison does not enter the body in that case.
inference: Under the condition established by the prior practice, poison does not enter the body even from bites by great serpents.
uncertainties: The condition from prior verses is presupposed but not repeated here.
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
